description: Still laying in stores for a hand that stopped coming. Crowd this brown handful of spines and the quills stay in.
lore: It travels the bottoms of things — walls, hedge-lines, the low sides of paths — on a route that stopped leading anywhere long ago, carrying a fistful of hard glossy kernels it cannot eat and will not be parted from. A hedgehog has no use for a nut. Behind this one was a person who put food out at a certain hour, and an animal that learned to be at the place when they did, and of that whole arrangement the piece that lasted is the being-there. It still arrives at the old hour, to a patch of grass where a doorstep used to be, and waits, and eats nothing, and moves on.

[[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] says the wall it keeps to on the old east road was a garden wall, and that he knows whose garden. He is not making it up; the road is his stock in trade, and he sells what he remembers of it for company. So the name this animal has been keeping its appointment with is not gone. It is sitting in an old man by a fire, one evening's listening from being said aloud, and nobody has paid the evening yet.

Crowd it and the quills go in barbed and stay in. Somewhere in the dark there is a black-pelted thing carrying three of them, from a meeting on the low side of a path that neither of them chose or understood. The [[monsters/white_rabbit|white rabbit]] keeps an hour of its own, out on open ground. The low country is full of them.
gm_notes: The garden-owner's name is unwritten on purpose: any GM may coin it at Wendell's fire (a leaf name, never cast). The one-evening price is a ready quest shape — sit with Wendell, learn the name, go say it on the hedgehog's patch at the hour. What that does is the GM's to decide.
